entityDescription:
Jenny Milne is based in Scotland but enjoys travel and as such has lived overseas and travelled around the globe and her energy and enthusiasm often earns her the reputation of being a ‘pocket rocket’. This description sums up well her enthusiasm and passion for social policy and transport. Very much an ‘out of the box’ thinker, Jenny is strategic and visionary and is well known for facilitating innovation and delivering on projects.

For those interested in the transport industry, having spent nearly 20years in the ITS and technology field, Jenny is currently involved in a number of projects, but one of growing interest to many is based upon the rural economy in Scotland. This originated from her first hand experiences from the last decade having a cottage in Boat of Garten which is based in the Cairngorms National Park. The area consists of 5 local authorities, 3 RTPs, several transport providers for bus, rail, community transport, taxi, cycle hire etc as well as community and business organisations. Until 2016 there was no joint partnership/board working towards a solution fit for visitors and residents alike. The challenges range from no 3G/GPRS, mountains and a fractured transport network. Jenny has brought together all the stakeholders from the ground level (community/businesses) to the top (Government organisations) together with the vision and determination to deliver Mobility as a Service. Given what’s already been said about the ‘pocket rocket’, it will be of no surprise to learn that Jenny took on a part time PhD in 2018 on Rural Mobility as a Service (R-MaaS) and in 2019 secured Innovate UK funding for Cairngorms Connected.Jenny was also involved in a project led byConnected Places Catapult in Aberdeenshire on understanding the need and demand for rural mobility services. Finally, Jenny is the founder of the Scottish Rural Islands and Transport Convention which has run since 2018 and focuses very much on mobility, economic growth and sustainability in rural areas both in the UK and overseas.

The technology design and development centre will be based in Southern England, close to the Formula 1 and space industry centres, while the test stands and spaceport-related operations will be based in South Wales, thereby bringing a major space entity and associated jobs to the Enterprise Zone in Port Talbot.
The initial intent is to produce space-ready tanks for integration into the Black Arrow launchers, placing 500 kg payloads into Polar or Sun Synchronous orbits. The Company will also attract products from many innovative SME's from around Europe and act as an attractive flight bed for new technologies.
The primary USP of Black Arrow will be the adoption of a seaborne spaceport: two vessels that will comprise the launch fleet, with a launch location off the South West of Ireland. The seaborne operation provides many advantages over the traditional land-based spaceports, notably: low-cost and low-impact establishment of the spaceport; low-risk to the public, property and critical infrastructure due to avoidance of land overflight, disruption of air corridors, and overflight of populated areas; low-emissions by utilising readily available cryogenic propellants, in the propulsion of vessels and vehicles. From this location, trajectories can be supported to North or South. After demonstration of the small launch system is complete, the same design approach will be used to scale-up the launch vehicles and the fleet to provide a larger lift capacity and allow the fleet to offer a launch service around the world, for friendly nations who would otherwise not be able to provide local launch services to be able to do so. This offering will be a very popular offering in various places and disrupt the established land-based market for small launchers.

Crypta Labs is a London-based quantum security company with the ambition to build futureproof hardware to provide secure communications for connected IoT devices everywhere.

Crypta Labs has designed a Quantum Random Number Generator (QRNG) with real world applications in mind. Every cryptographic task requires a source of random numbers, which means weak randomness equals weak cryptography. Our QRNG has passed all the randomness tests from NIST and TestU01 suites, unlike some of the competitors on the market today.

We have also developed a Hardware Security Module (HSM), designed for use in connected autonomous vehicles (CAV). The HSM can perform a range of cryptographic tasks including key generation and management and will be an EU mandated requirement within both the vehicle and infrastructure as C-ITS is adopted. The HSM was designed in accordance with the European Commissions’ Security Policy and is currently used in the Czech Republic’s participation in the CRoads pilot scheme. 

We are currently integrating our QRNG technology into the HSM, using its quantum random numbers to seed cryptographic operations. The QHSM will provide reliable cryptographic support seeded by high-quality random numbers at a local level.
